page: Microsoft Azure E48as_v5 is an EASv5-family virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, it features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The processor runs at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz and includes 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. No local storage is bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable, and it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core and single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng scores of 64784.93 and 2726.67 respectively. Cryptographic capabilities are also strong, as evidenced by a PassMark CPU encryption score of 51361.84. Memory performance is robust, with a PassMark memory score of 2903.87, while large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 83.85 GB/sec. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench ray tracing and image processing benchmarks also place in the top 25%. However, the instance exhibits average performance in database operations, Redis SET operations, and software compilation. Large-scale LLM text generation is a notable bottleneck, with the 70B model text generation speed falling into the bottom 10% at 2.31 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E48as_v5 offers high memory density relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require dedicated GPU acceleration. The primary hardware tradeoff is the complete absence of local storage, requiring users to provision external Premium Storage. This configuration is suited for memory-bound applications, enterprise databases, multi-threaded data decompression, image processing, and intermediate-scale language model inference.
